title: Ordinary derived scalar associators and point sections-tensor tower coherence
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and finite extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$ with valuation rings [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary K-flat derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on sheaf-module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\theta^D$ be the natural sections-tensor comparison of [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent]. For $K\in D(R_E)$ put $A=K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$, let $\alpha:(K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)\otimes^L_{R_L}R_M\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_M$ be the canonical ordinary derived scalar associator, and let $a^{\mathrm{mod}}$ be the module-complex associator. Then
$$\Gamma(s,\alpha)\circ\theta^D_{M/L,A}\circ(\theta^D_{L/E,K}\otimes1)=\theta^D_{M/E,K}\circ a^{\mathrm{mod}}.$$

This equation holds on cochain representatives and in derived categories, naturally for all derived morphisms. On a K-flat flat-term representative $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $P\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ is K-flat with flat terms and represents $A$; $\alpha$ and its inverse are represented by the balanced sheaf maps $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes ab$ and $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. The common sections map in the displayed equation sends $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to the section $n\otimes ab$. The associator is natural also on arbitrary derived roofs. For $L=E$, the multiplication maps $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$ on sheaf complexes and $n\otimes r\mapsto rn$ on module complexes intertwine $\theta^D_{E/E,K}$. For four finite fields $E\subset L\subset M\subset H$, the two iterated ordinary scalar associators agree, and every iterated sections comparison is compatible with them: the resulting map on a representative sends $(((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $n\otimes abc$. These unit and iterated equations are independent of all chosen resolutions. These assertions concern ordinary derived tensors, with no completion comparison or integral scalar-extension functor in the conclusion.

proof.text: Write $T_{V/U}C=C\otimes_{R_U}R_V$ and $t_{V/U}N=N\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal O_V$ on complexes. For each pair in the tower, [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor] identifies coefficient sections with their valuation rings compatibly with inclusions and gives the natural chain isomorphism $\theta_{V/U,C}(n\otimes a)=n\otimes a_s$. By [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], $T$, $t$ and $\Gamma(s,-)$ preserve all quasi-isomorphisms; the localization of $T_{V/U}$ is identified with the stipulated ordinary derived scalar extension by its counit. The localization of this particular $\theta$ is exactly the stipulated $\theta^D$. These statements apply to every complex, including the intermediate $T_{L/E}C$, without a completeness or boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; specialization through the two cited point-sections comparison statements

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$, define $u_F: (F\otimes_{R_E}R_L)\otimes_{R_L}R_M\to F\otimes_{R_E}R_M$ by $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes ab$, using the coefficient inclusions. The inner balance is respected because $(rx)\otimes ab=x\otimes r(ab)$, and the outer balance because $x\otimes(ac)b=x\otimes a(cb)$. Its inverse is $v_F(x\otimes b)=(x\otimes1)\otimes b$: the $R_E$-balance follows from $((rx)\otimes1)\otimes b=(x\otimes r)\otimes b=(x\otimes1)\otimes rb$. These compatible bilinear formulas define sheaf maps by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the unique factorization in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], applied successively to the two tensor factors. They are $R_M$-linear. The composites are the identity, since $(x\otimes1)\otimes ab=(x\otimes a)\otimes b$. Equalities are tested before each sheafification by its uniqueness clause; no assertion that all global sections of a sheaf tensor are pure is needed. Applying the identical balanced formulas to ordinary modules defines $a^{\mathrm{mod}}$ and its inverse. All formulas commute with restrictions and with $f(x)$ for a module-sheaf map $f$.

proof.text: Apply $u$ and $v$ degreewise to any cochain complex $C$. The differential check is $d(x\otimes ab)=dx\otimes ab=u((dx\otimes a)\otimes b)$; the inverse check is the same with $a=1$. Coefficients are in degree zero, so no Koszul signs occur. The maps are natural chain isomorphisms. To compute the derived version, choose $P\to C$ K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to the identity morphism of the underlying sheaf topos and the ring map $R_E\to R_L$. The inverse image is the identity (hence preserves finite limits), so its module pullback is precisely $T_{L/E}$. Thus $T_{L/E}P$ is K-flat with flat terms. Take the small-site presentation in the fixed larger module universe used for these sheaf-module categories. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], both successive derived extensions and direct extension to $R_M$ are consequently computed by these very complexes. Their canonical scalar-composition associator is the class of $u_P$, with inverse the class of $v_P$, as in the K-flat construction of derived pullback composition.

proof.text: On $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)$ in degree $i$ of $t_{M/L}t_{L/E}\Gamma(s,C)$, the upper route first gives $(n\otimes a_s)\otimes b_s$ and then the section $n\otimes a_sb_s=n\otimes(ab)_s$. The lower route first gives $n\otimes ab$ and then the same section, by [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]. Equality extends to the whole module by additivity and the two tensor balancing relations. The maps commute with differentials by the previous step and by the chain assertion of the cited node. Thus $\Gamma(s,u_C)\theta_{M/L,T_{L/E}C}(\theta_{L/E,C}\otimes1)=\theta_{M/E,C}a^{\mathrm{mod}}$ is an equality of natural chain maps for every $C$, in particular every $P$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], every composite functor occurring in the last equation preserves quasi-isomorphisms before the final localization. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2) to the natural chain isomorphisms $u,v,\theta$ after composing with target localization. They descend to natural isomorphisms, and (2)-(3) preserve compositions and equality. Conjugate by the counit-fixed comparisons of [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent]. Step 3 identifies the descended $u$ with $\alpha$ on K-flat representatives, and that descent identifies the descended $\theta$ with $\theta^D$ on every representative. The equation of step 4 therefore becomes exactly the displayed derived equation, with its stated source and target.

proof.text: For clarity, the associator's naturality on a roof $C\xleftarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{f}J$ can be checked without choosing a lift between resolutions. Put $F=T_{M/L}T_{L/E}$ and $G=T_{M/E}$, and denote localized chain maps by the same letters. Chain naturality gives $G(f)u_H=u_JF(f)$ and $G(q)u_H=u_CF(q)$. Since $F(q),G(q)$ are invertible by [lem-weil-point-derived-sections-tensor-descent], the latter gives $G(q)^{-1}u_C=u_HF(q)^{-1}$, and substitution yields $G(f)G(q)^{-1}u_C=u_JF(f)F(q)^{-1}$. The same algebra applies to $\theta$ and to the unit maps below. Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes each descent unique with its representative comparison; thus any K-flat resolution computes this same transformation. Replacing resolutions cannot change either the maps or their equations.

proof.text: For the equal-field case define $m_F:F\otimes_{R_E}R_E\to F$ by $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$; its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Balance and $R_E$-linearity show both composites are identities. The module multiplication map has the identical formula. On a section tensor $n\otimes r$, $\Gamma(s,m_F)\theta_{E/E,F}$ gives $r_sn=rn$, using the coefficient-section identification of [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor]. Hence it equals module multiplication, degreewise, naturally in complexes. This is the requested unit equation. Under the descent of step 5 it is the unit equation for $\theta^D$; the representative-normalized comparisons ensure the prescribed multiplication identifications are the ones being used.

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset M\subset H$, apply the already constructed $u$ to a nested sheaf tensor $(((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c)$. One composition gives $x\otimes(ab)c$, and the other $x\otimes a(bc)$; these are equal by associativity in $R_H$. Repeated uniqueness of the balanced maps of step 2 gives equality as sheaf chain maps. For module tensors the same calculation gives $n\otimes abc$. Repeated use of [lem-weil-point-finite-free-sections-tensor] sends $a,b,c$ to their constant sections, whose product is $(abc)_s$; consequently the iterated sections comparisons give that same section whichever route is chosen. The localization theorem [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] carries these equalities to derived categories. Step 6 supplies their resolution independence. This includes identity stages and repeated fields, and proves precisely ordinary scalar-tower coherence.
